title: Fantasy Foosball Year 8, 2026: Week 4 Preview
subtitle: With six playoff spots available, early-season modeled odds remain volatile across the standings.

playoffModel.description: Seeded Monte Carlo estimate using current record, scoring strength and remaining Sleeper schedule.

matchups.headline: Payton faces a steep climb against unbeaten Kane
matchups.paragraph: Payton’s I ♥️ Big Tet-Tees enters Week 4 ranked eighth at 1-2, while Kane’s Blueballs sits first at 3-0. The model gives Payton a 39.3% playoff chance, rising to 52.8% with a win and falling to 32.5% with a loss—a 20.3-point swing. Kane’s modeled chance is already 98.6%, moving only to 99.5% with victory or 96.9% with defeat. Payton, a two-time champion in 2020 and 2021, needs the larger odds movement in this matchup.

matchups.headline: Unbeaten Andy meets a high-leverage test for Parker
matchups.paragraph: Andy’s Long dong silvers are 3-0 and ranked second, giving Andy a 90.8% modeled playoff chance before facing Parker. Parker’s My BallDak hurts is 1-2 and ranked seventh, with a 41.1% chance. A win would move Andy to 95.6% and Parker to 53.2%; a loss would put them at 84.7% and 31.4%, respectively. Parker’s 21.8-point swing is larger than Andy’s 10.9, making this especially important for the 2019 inaugural champion and league Public Enemy.

matchups.headline: Kade has the edge, but Brae needs movement now
matchups.paragraph: Kade’s CheesusJesus is ranked sixth at 2-1, while Brae’s Ogles Outlaws are 11th at 0-3. The model gives Kade a 43.6% playoff chance, with a win lifting that estimate to 51.2% and a loss dropping it to 29.3%, a 21.9-point swing. Brae’s modeled chance is just 0.5%, changing to 1% with victory or 0.2% with defeat. Early-season odds can be volatile, but this matchup offers Kade meaningful leverage while Brae remains a substantial long shot.

matchups.headline: Former champions meet at the bottom of the model
matchups.paragraph: Joey’s Off Constantly is ranked 12th at 0-3, and Cooper’s Jack MeHoff is 10th at 1-2. Joey’s modeled playoff chance is 0.1%, rising to 0.2% with a win and reaching 0% with a loss. Cooper starts at 3%, with the model moving him to 4.4% after victory or 1% after defeat, a 3.4-point swing. The stakes are modest in modeled terms, and the early-season estimates remain volatile, though both managers bring championship history: Joey won in 2024 and Cooper in 2022.

matchups.headline: Evan and Alex clash in a ranked 2-1 matchup
matchups.paragraph: Evan’s Bonnie Blue 42 and Alex’s I love big TD’s are both 2-1, ranked fourth and fifth, respectively. The model gives Evan a 94.2% playoff chance, compared with 70.2% for Alex. A win moves Evan to 96.9% and Alex to 81.7%; a loss moves them to 89.6% and 63.4%. Alex’s modeled swing is 18.3 points, versus 7.3 for Evan. Evan is the 2023 champion, while Alex won in 2025, adding league-history context to a meaningful early-season meeting.

matchups.headline: Third-ranked CJ can widen the gap over Kohlt
matchups.paragraph: CJ’s cjbroadway23 is ranked third at 2-1, while Kohlt’s kohlt is ninth at 1-2. CJ enters with a 95.3% modeled playoff chance, rising to 97.9% with a win and falling to 89.2% with a loss. Kohlt’s chance is 23.4%, moving to 35.9% after victory or 18.1% after defeat. Kohlt therefore carries the larger modeled swing at 17.8 points, compared with CJ’s 8.7. With six playoff spots, the early-season estimates still warrant some volatility caution.
